item.text: {"text":"NextItNet’s stacked causal dilated convolutions and residual blocks expand the history accessible to each prediction ([original paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)). For stride-one convolutions, the theoretical receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σ(kℓ−1)dℓ, counting every temporal convolution. Proposed diagnostic: preserve the last s interactions while swapping equal-length prefixes between users within the same category; sweep s across dilation/receptive-field boundaries. Prefix changes entirely outside the receptive field should leave final-position scores unchanged, assuming position-local normalization and no global aggregation. Recent explanation research supports history interventions: [2025 counterfactual explanations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal edits changing recommendations; [2025 FCESR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13632) examines sufficiency and necessity. These motivate probes but do not establish a NextItNet-specific padding or suffix-swap protocol.\n\nRecommended controls: compare recent-item replacement, recent-order shuffling, suffix-only histories, and matched-size older-history perturbations. Keep positions fixed for replacement/shuffle tests; report deletion separately because compaction changes temporal distances. Test padding invariance by adding leading padding without truncating real interactions, with dropout disabled; compare scores at the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Nonzero differences can reveal padding propagation, normalization, or indexing effects. Measure target-rank change, target-versus-negative margins, top-10 overlap, and paired validation HR@10 changes using identical pinned candidates. Sensitivity alone does not demonstrate useful personalization: stronger evidence requires intact histories to outperform perturbed histories on held-out validation targets. Report paired uncertainty and category results alongside the four-category macro average; interpret perturbations as model-behavior tests, not proof of users’ causal intent."}
